To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Maternal embryonic leucin zipper kinase is a host factor that promotes HIV-1 cDN A synthesis, (2) MELK phosphorylates the capsid protein at Serine-149, (3) MELK is an attractive target for HIV-1 therapy.
the host factor maternal embryonic leukaemia kinase is a novel host factor that is required for efficient HIV- 1 replication.
MELK phosphorylates the capsid to promote HIV-1 cDNAsynthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of HIV-1 cDNAsynthesis after entry.
the mechanisms of the HIV life cycle, and in particular with HIV-1 capsids and their interactions with host cell factors, which is important for the design of novel anti-HIV-1 therapies.
the regulation of HIV-1 uncoating by the host factor MELK and the development of MELK inhibitors to prevent the uncoating of HIV-1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our data reveal a previously unrecognized host factor that regulates HIV-1 capsids to promote uncoating, thereby facilitating the initiation of viral cDNA synthesis.
MELK phosphorylates HIV-1 capsids to promote uncoating and cDNA synthesis.
MELK phosphorylates the HIV-1 CA protein at serine 149 and promotes the uncoating of HIV-1, thereby enhancing viral cDNA synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel host factor MELK required for HIV-1 capsids to uncoating and promote viral cDNA formation.
HIV-1 capsids undergo phosphorylation-dependent conformational changes that are critical for the uncoating of HIV-1 core.
HIV-1 capsids are disassembled by phosphorylation of capsid proteins, and the phosphorylation is catalyzed by MELK.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MELK phosphorylates the capsid to promote HIV-1 cDNAsynthesis, and this process is critical for HIV-1 replication.
we have identified the maternal embryonic leukaemia kinase (MEL) as an important regulator of HIV-1 infection.
